question: My 1/1 creature with undying has a +1/+1 counter on it. A spell puts three -1/-1 counters on it at once. The counters cancel down to two -1/-1 counters left over, so the creature dies from having 0 or less toughness. Does undying trigger, since the creature technically still had a +1/+1 counter on it before all this happened?

expected.shortAnswer: No: undying does not trigger, because it last had a +1/+1 counter on the battlefield.
expected.answer: You control Young Wolf, a 1/1 creature with undying, and it has a +1/+1 counter on it. A spell puts three -1/-1 counters on Young Wolf. Before state-based actions are performed, Young Wolf has one +1/+1 counter and three -1/-1 counters on it. After state-based actions are performed, Young Wolf is in the graveyard. When it was last on the battlefield, it had a +1/+1 counter on it, so undying will not trigger.

whyHard: The counter-cancellation state-based action (rule 704.5q) and the 0-toughness state-based action happen at the same time, so the creature's last known information is taken from before EITHER of them resolved -- meaning the +1/+1 counter still counts against undying's "had no +1/+1 counters" trigger condition, which is easy to miss if you assume the counters cancel first and the creature dies a step later.
